question_text: You are driving on a road with one lane in each direction and want to turn left. Where should you position yourself?

options.text: - towards the centre of the roadway
- on the right-hand edge of the roadway

correct_answers.text: - towards the centre of the roadway

comment: When turning left in this situation, go towards the center of the road (which is the left side of your lane)

question_text: Are you allowed to use your motorized bicycle on the pavement?

options.text: Yes, if the motorized bicycle is cautiously pushed
Yes, if the motorized bicycle is used as a bicycle
Yes, also using the engine when traffic on the roadway is too dense

correct_answers.text: Yes, if the motorized bicycle is cautiously pushed

comment: Yes but only if you push it, you cannot ride on the pavement

question_text: Several cars are waiting in the right-hand lane at a "red" traffic light. Are you allowed to pass the cars cautiously on the right?

options.text: Yes, provided there is adequate space on the roadway
Yes, provided you use the pavement
No, you must always wait behind the last car

correct_answers.text: Yes, provided there is adequate space on the roadway

comment: In this case you can behave similarly to a bicycle and can pass the car on the right if there is enough space

question_text: You are driving on a road outside a built-up area with three lanes marked in each direction. Individual slower vehicles are travelling well spaced out in the right-hand lane. Which lane may you use continuously?

options.text: The middle lane
The left-hand lane

correct_answers.text: The middle lane

comment: The left-hand lane may only be used by a car driver for the temporary overtaking of other vehicles. Continuous driving on the middle lane is permitted, however, if the road is located outside built-up areas and provided with a line marking. This also applies if only a few vehicles are on the right lane.

question_text: What risks could arise if you drive in the right-hand lane alongside a truck?

options.text: - be overlooked by the driver of the truck
- be overlooked by other road users
- overlook other road users

correct_answers.text: - be overlooked by the driver of the truck
- be overlooked by other road users
- overlook other road users

comment: A truck will diminish both your visibility and other people on the road seeing you (including the driver of the truck)

question_text: What applies to you at the next junction?

options.text: - turn left
- turn right
- drive straight ahead

correct_answers.text: - turn left
- turn right

question_text: You would like to turn right. What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I remain behind the [blue car]
I drive up to the stop line
I drive up to the line of sight

correct_answers.text: I remain behind the [blue car]

comment: A motorcycle should behave similarly to a car and wait behind the blue car.

question_text: What cycle paths may you use to drive your moped?

options.text: Cycle paths outside of a built-up area
Cycle paths within a built-up area, if this is permitted by an additional sign
Cycle paths within a built-up area, if there is too much traffic on the road

correct_answers.text: Cycle paths outside of a built-up area
Cycle paths within a built-up area, if this is permitted by an additional sign

comment: You may ride your moped on cycle paths outside built-up areas and on cycle paths inside built-up areas if an additional sign permits this.

question_text: What is the correct course of action on this one-way road?

options.text: I wait until the works enable me to drive past
I turn around and drive back
I reverse back up the road

correct_answers.text: I wait until the works enable me to drive past

comment: You only drive on when the work allows it. In a one-way street, you are only allowed to drive in one direction. You are not allowed to turn around or reverse. You are responsible for any accident that may occur.

question_text: For which motor vehicles or combination vehicles designated or used for road haulage purposes, is it necessary to pay a user charge on federal highways?

options.text: For motor vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating of at least 7.5 t
For combination vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating of at least 7.5 t
For combination vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating less than 7.5 t

correct_answers.text: For motor vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating of at least 7.5 t
For combination vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating of at least 7.5 t

comment: For motor vehicles with a maximum authorized mass of at least 7.5 t and combinations of vehicles with a maximum authorized mass of at least 7.5 tons must be paid a usage fee (toll).

question_text: What motor vehicles and combination vehicles are subject to a toll charge on motorways and federal highways?

options.text: - are used in road haulage operations
- have a gross vehicle weight rating of at least 7.5 t
- have at least 4 seats

correct_answers.text: - are used in road haulage operations
- have a gross vehicle weight rating of at least 7.5 t

comment: Motor vehicles and vehicle combinations to a maximum authorized mass of at least 7.5 t have, are toll roads. The same applies to vehicles that are used for freight transport.

question_text: You are transporting hazardous goods during winter. What should you do if road conditions deteriorate due to packed snow?

options.text: - ensure that no-one else is endangered
- look for the next suitable place to stop and park, if necessary
- always transport hazardous goods to the destination with no intermediate stops

correct_answers.text: - ensure that no-one else is endangered
- look for the next suitable place to stop and park, if necessary

comment: In icy weather, you must take special care to avoid endangering others. If you reach a point where you can no longer guarantee that others will not be endangered, you should find a good place to park.

question_text: You are driving an agricultural tractor at 30 km/h on a main road with a paved hard shoulder on the right. What is the right thing to do?

options.text: I have to drive on the hard shoulder when possible
I may only use the hard shoulder for stopping
I may only use the hard shoulder briefly to allow vehicles to overtake

correct_answers.text: I have to drive on the hard shoulder when possible

comment: In order to continue to ensure the flow of traffic, please go possible on the shoulder of your agricultural tractor.

question_text: What risks could arise if you drive in the right-hand lane alongside a truck?

options.text: - be unseen
- overlook other road users
- get burned by the hot exhaust fumes from the truck

correct_answers.text: - be unseen
- overlook other road users

comment: A truck will diminish both your visibility and other people on the road seeing you (including the driver of the truck)
